key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures do more than reduce reflection in perovskite solar cells: they also improve wetting, crystallinity, charge extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Using textured interfaces is a multi-functional design strategy that can simultaneously boost efficiency, film quality, and device durability in perovskite photovoltaics and related optoelectronics.
method: Review of recently reported texture-related effects in perovskite-based solar cells.
Focus on benefits beyond light management, including wetting, crystallinity, carrier extraction, and stress handling.
Synthesis of findings across solar cells, photodetectors, and LEDs.
evidence_signal: The abstract summarizes recent reported studies qualitatively and does not provide a single new experimental dataset or benchmark in the text provided.
watch_item: Texture benefits may depend strongly on fabrication route and device stack, so improvements in one metric can be offset by process complexity or nonuniformity.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
